mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a supply-driven inflation scare that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid 0.5 percentage point rise in the unemployment rate over 3 months, if accompanied by a contemporaneous decline in consumer spending, signals a labor market shock that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months and RSAFS declines
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (UMCSENT) rises during the signal period, indicating the labor market shock is transitory and will not materially impact spending.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point hike in the federal funds rate, if not already at a restrictive level (> 4%), signals a tightening monetary cycle that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month and level < 4%
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month rise in housing starts, if accompanied by a contemporaneous decline in the unemployment rate, signals a strengthening labor market and increased consumer spending power that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE declines
failure_condition: Yield curve flattens significantly (10y-2y spread < 0.5%) during the signal period, indicating waning economic momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp 1% rise in the consumer price index over 3 months, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in industrial production, signals a cost-push inflation scare that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 1% in 3 months and INDPRO does not rise
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid 1% decline in payroll employment over 3 months, if accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in the federal funds rate, signals a policy-induced labor market shock that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 1% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS rises
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) decline during the signal period, indicating the labor market shock is transitory and will not materially impact employment.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point cut in the federal funds rate, if already at an accommodative level (< 2%), signals an easing monetary cycle that will boost risk appetite and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.5pp in 1 month and level < 2%
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.
